correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts every factorization type allowed by \(\Omega(n),\Omega(n+2)\le2\). The even branch leaves only \(n=4\); the odd mixed prime, square, and semiprime types are eliminated by exact totient identities and one elementary AM-GM bound. In the remaining squarefree-semiprime branch, equal totients and the gap \(2\) force \(r+s=p+q+2\); the difference-of-squares identity then gives unique odd parameters \(A,B\), from which all four primes are recovered exactly. The converse identities \(rs=pq+2\) and \(r+s=p+q+2\) return equal totients. The finite checker independently reproduces every low-\(\Omega\) solution through \(10^6\) but is explicitly non-probative for the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The fixed-gap equation \(\varphi(n)=\varphi(n+2)\) is a long-studied open arithmetic problem. Bounding both endpoints by \(\Omega\le2\) is the canonical first nontrivial multiplicative-complexity layer, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The theorem closes that whole layer, separates the two prime-power exceptions from the genuinely composite-composite branch, and converts every remaining solution into a unique four-prime bilinear parameter set. This gives a reusable structural description rather than a table recomputation.
